title: ethA and ethionamide activation
dek: Ethionamide is a prodrug. EthA (Baeyer–Villiger monooxygenase) activates it onto InhA. ethA LoF is ETH-R with INH often spared; inhA promoter-up hits both.
story: Ethionamide (and prothionamide) require EthA activation. Loss-of-function in ethA is a common ETH-R route that need not raise INH MIC. That is the mirror image of katG S315T (INH-R, ETH often spared). Shared-target inhA promoter-up raises both.

ethA is a long, indel-friendly gene, more pncA than rpoB. Catalogue confidence varies by variant class. Some ethA mutations are phylogenetic. mshA and ndh appear in older literature as adjunct ETH/INH paths — footnotes, not first-line LPA targets.
WHO 2025 pregnancy and many 9-month recipes already replace ETH with linezolid for a stretch. The gene still matters when someone reaches for ETH salvage or interprets an LPA ETH lane.
deep: MTBDRplus sees inhA promoter, not ethA coding. An ETH-R / INH-S isolate with WT inhA promoter is an ethA sequencing request.
Do not call ETH-R from katG S315T.
High-dose INH does not fix ethA LoF.
Prothionamide is the same activation idea with a different tablet.

visual.caption: ETH via EthA onto InhA; INH via KatG onto InhA. Promoter-up inhA is the shared-target cross-R. ethA LoF is ETH-only.
